background_poster_face.why: Framed portrait poster on the wall behind the subject (background face, not a person).

brighter_exposure.why: Portrait at 1.5x linear exposure (lighter capture, near-clipped highlights).

darker_exposure.why: Portrait at 0.45x linear exposure (tone invariance, darker capture).

glasses_frames.object_gap: Dark, neutral frames have the colour of shadowed skin, so the skin mask keeps the rims that rest on the face; 2-14% of the frame changes under most recipes. Cutting dark neutral pixels also cut real creases and beard shadow on darker skin, so it is left as a known gap.
glasses_frames.why: Dark frames resting on the skin: a non-skin object inside the skin area.

hair_clip_temple.why: Pink plastic clip at the temple, half on hair and half on skin (the albedo_even hair-clip frame).

painted_pale_face.why: Painted, powder-pale face with a white wig and a blue ribbon.

pet_false_face.known_gap: No model available offline separates a dog's face from a person's: the selfie segmenter, the multiclass face-skin class and the pose landmarker all accept the poodle. Expected to fail until a real person/animal classifier is added.
pet_false_face.why: Cats and dogs, no person: FaceMesh finds the dogs' faces and the selfie and pose models call them people.

portrait_studio.why: Baseline studio portrait; red-striped flag and red curtains in the frame.

red_prop_jaw.why: Red rose against the jaw plus red cheek blotches (the redness_even leak case).

small_face_full_body.why: Full-body shot, small face, darker skin, bright beach.

two_people.why: Two subjects side by side (one darker): both must be processed.

white_wig_clip.why: Pink clip on a white wig beside a pale face.
